html: //! Reads a Zig file's declarations and identifiers with `std.zig.Ast` and the //! tokenizer, for `zig_decls`, `zig_rename`, `zig_move` and `zig_imports`. Pure: //! source in, answer out. The analysis is syntax and tokens, not types. const std = @import("std"); const Ast = std.zig.Ast; /// What a declaration is, by its leading keyword; `field` is a container field. pub const Kind = enum { @"fn", @"const", @"var", @"test", @"comptime", field }; /// How a declaration is named: `identifier` (a declaration, a field, /// `test foo {}`), `string` (`test "..."`, named by the string's text) or /// `none` (`test {}`, `comptime`, named `""`). pub const NameForm = enum { identifier, string, none }; /// Lines, 1-based, inclusive. pub const Lines = struct { first: usize, last: usize }; /// A declaration of a container's top level. Its span runs from its doc /// comment to the `}`, `;` or (for a field) `,` that ends it. pub const Decl = struct { kind: Kind, /// The name's text; `""` when `name_form` is `none`. name: []const u8, name_form: NameForm, /// A field is always `pub`. visibility: enum { @"pub", file }, linkage: enum { none, @"extern", @"export" }, /// First line of the span, 1-based. first: usize, /// Last line of the span, 1-based, inclusive. last: usize, /// Byte offset of the span's start, inclusive. start: usize, /// Byte offset of the span's end, exclusive. stop: usize, /// The plain `//` lines directly above the span, if any. comment_above: ?Lines, /// The line its name is on (for a test or a comptime, its first token's). name_line: usize = 0, /// A `const`'s or `var`'s value, as its source says it; else "". value: []const u8 = "", /// When its value is a container, the names of its members that are not /// `pub`: what `X.y` from another file needs `pub` on. Fields are not listed. private_members: []const []const u8 = &.{}, }; /// Declarations read, and the tokens and nodes it took (the charge). pub const Read = struct { decls: []const Decl, tokens: usize, nodes: usize }; /// The declarations, or the line and tag of the parser's first error; never a /// partial list. pub const Decls = union(enum) { ok: Read, parse_error: struct { line: usize, tag: []const u8 }, }; /// A file's top-level declarations, in file order. pub fn decls(a: std.mem.Allocator, src: [:0]const u8) error{OutOfMemory}!Decls { const tree = try Ast.parse(a, src, .{ .mode = .zig }); if (tree.errors.len != 0) { const e = tree.errors[0]; return .{ .parse_error = .{ .line = tree.tokenLocation(0, e.token).line + 1, .tag = @tagName(e.tag) } }; } const starts = try lineStarts(a, src); var out: std.ArrayList(Decl) = .empty; for (tree.rootDecls()) |n| try out.append(a, try declOf(a, &tree, src, starts, n)); return .{ .ok = .{ .decls = out.items, .tokens = tree.tokens.len, .nodes = tree.nodes.len } }; } /// The members of a container, or why there are none to give. pub const Members = union(enum) { ok: Read, parse_error: struct { line: usize, tag: []const u8 }, /// No top-level `const name = struct/union/enum/opaque {...}` by that name. no_container: void, }; /// The declarations and fields of the top-level `const name = struct {...}` (or /// union, enum, opaque), in order, read as the top level is. Used by /// `zig_decls(p, {container = name})`. pub fn members(a: std.mem.Allocator, src: [:0]const u8, name: []const u8) error{OutOfMemory}!Members { const tree = try Ast.parse(a, src, .{ .mode = .zig }); if (tree.errors.len != 0) { const e = tree.errors[0]; return .{ .parse_error = .{ .line = tree.tokenLocation(0, e.token).line + 1, .tag = @tagName(e.tag) } }; } const starts = try lineStarts(a, src); for (tree.rootDecls()) |n| { const vd = tree.fullVarDecl(n) orelse continue; if (!std.mem.eql(u8, tree.tokenSlice(vd.ast.mut_token + 1), name)) continue; const init = vd.ast.init_node.unwrap() orelse continue; var buf: [2]Ast.Node.Index = undefined; const c = tree.fullContainerDecl(&buf, init) orelse continue; var out: std.ArrayList(Decl) = .empty; for (c.ast.members) |m| try out.append(a, try declOf(a, &tree, src, starts, m)); return .{ .ok = .{ .decls = out.items, .tokens = tree.tokens.len, .nodes = tree.nodes.len } }; } return .no_container; } /// One declaration, from its node: its kind, name, visibility, linkage and /// span (its doc comment to its `;`, `}` or field's `,`). fn declOf(a: std.mem.Allocator, tree: *const Ast, src: [:0]const u8, starts: []const usize, n: Ast.Node.Index) error{OutOfMemory}!Decl { var d: Decl = .{ .kind = .@"const", .name = "", .name_form = .identifier, .visibility = .file, .linkage = .none, .first = 0, .last = 0, .start = 0, .stop = 0, .comment_above = null }; switch (tree.nodeTag(n)) { .fn_decl, .fn_proto, .fn_proto_multi, .fn_proto_one, .fn_proto_simple => { var buf: [1]Ast.Node.Index = undefined; const fp = tree.fullFnProto(&buf, n).?; d.kind = .@"fn"; if (fp.name_token) |t| { d.name = tree.tokenSlice(t); d.name_line = lineOf(starts, tree.tokenStart(t)); } else d.name_form = .none; if (fp.visib_token != null) d.visibility = .@"pub"; if (fp.extern_export_inline_token) |t| d.linkage = linkageOf(tree.tokenTag(t)); }, .global_var_decl, .local_var_decl, .simple_var_decl, .aligned_var_decl => { const vd = tree.fullVarDecl(n).?; d.kind = if (tree.tokenTag(vd.ast.mut_token) == .keyword_const) .@"const" else .@"var"; d.name = tree.tokenSlice(vd.ast.mut_token + 1); d.name_line = lineOf(starts, tree.tokenStart(vd.ast.mut_token + 1)); if (vd.visib_token != null) d.visibility = .@"pub"; if (vd.extern_export_token) |t| d.linkage = linkageOf(tree.tokenTag(t)); if (vd.ast.init_node.unwrap()) |init| { const last_init = tree.lastToken(init); d.value = src[tree.tokenStart(tree.firstToken(init)) .. tree.tokenStart(last_init) + tree.tokenSlice(last_init).len]; d.private_members = try privateMembers(a, tree, init); } }, .test_decl => { d.kind = .@"test"; if (tree.nodeData(n).opt_token_and_node[0].unwrap()) |t| { const s = tree.tokenSlice(t); if (tree.tokenTag(t) == .string_literal) { d.name_form = .string; d.name = s[1 .. s.len - 1]; } else d.name = s; } else d.name_form = .none; }, .@"comptime" => { d.kind = .@"comptime"; d.name_form = .none; }, .container_field_init, .container_field_align, .container_field => { const cf = tree.fullContainerField(n).?; d.kind = .field; d.visibility = .@"pub"; d.name = tree.tokenSlice(cf.ast.main_token); }, // A container's members are nothing else. else => unreachable, } // Widen the span back over its doc comment and on to its `;` or `,`. var first = tree.firstToken(n); while (first > 0 and tree.tokenTag(first - 1) == .doc_comment) first -= 1; var last = tree.lastToken(n); if (last + 1 < tree.tokens.len) switch (tree.tokenTag(last + 1)) { .semicolon => last += 1, .comma => if (d.kind == .field) { last += 1; }, else => {}, }; if (d.name_line == 0) d.name_line = lineOf(starts, tree.tokenStart(tree.firstToken(n))); d.start = tree.tokenStart(first); d.stop = tree.tokenStart(last) + tree.tokenSlice(last).len; d.first = lineOf(starts, d.start); d.last = lineOf(starts, d.stop - 1); d.comment_above = commentAbove(src, starts, d.first); return d; } /// The names of a container value's declarations and functions that are not /// `pub`. fn privateMembers(a: std.mem.Allocator, tree: *const Ast, node: Ast.Node.Index) ![]const []const u8 { var buf: [2]Ast.Node.Index = undefined; const c = tree.fullContainerDecl(&buf, node) orelse return &.{}; var out: std.ArrayList([]const u8) = .empty; for (c.ast.members) |m| { var fb: [1]Ast.Node.Index = undefined; if (tree.fullVarDecl(m)) |vd| { if (vd.visib_token == null) try out.append(a, tree.tokenSlice(vd.ast.mut_token + 1)); } else if (tree.fullFnProto(&fb, m)) |fp| { if (fp.visib_token == null) if (fp.name_token) |t| try out.append(a, tree.tokenSlice(t)); } } return out.items; } fn linkageOf(tag: std.zig.Token.Tag) @FieldType(Decl, "linkage") { return switch (tag) { .keyword_extern => .@"extern", .keyword_export => .@"export", else => .none, }; } /// Where each line starts: `starts[i]` is line `i + 1`'s first byte. pub fn lineStarts(a: std.mem.Allocator, src: []const u8) ![]const usize { var out: std.ArrayList(usize) = .empty; try out.append(a, 0); for (src, 0..) |c, i| if (c == '\n') try out.append(a, i + 1); return out.items; } /// The line, 1-based, of the byte at `offset`. pub fn lineOf(starts: []const usize, offset: usize) usize { var lo: usize = 0; var hi: usize = starts.len; while (hi - lo > 1) { const mid = (lo + hi) / 2; if (starts[mid] <= offset) lo = mid else hi = mid; } return lo + 1; } /// The plain `//` lines directly above line `first` (no blank line /// between, not `///` or `//!`), or null. fn commentAbove(src: []const u8, starts: []const usize, first: usize) ?Lines { var top = first; while (top > 1) { const l = top - 1; const end = if (l < starts.len) starts[l] - 1 else src.len; const text = std.mem.trimStart(u8, src[starts[l - 1]..end], " \t"); if (!std.mem.startsWith(u8, text, "//") or std.mem.startsWith(u8, text, "///") or std.mem.startsWith(u8, text, "//!")) break; top = l; } return if (top == first) null else .{ .first = top, .last = first - 1 }; } pub const Tag = std.zig.Token.Tag; /// A token's tag and byte range. pub const Tok = struct { tag: Tag, start: usize, end: usize }; /// A file's tokens, or the line of the first one Zig's tokenizer refuses. pub fn tokens(a: std.mem.Allocator, src: [:0]const u8) error{OutOfMemory}!union(enum) { ok: []const Tok, invalid: usize } { var toks: std.ArrayList(Tok) = .empty; var tz = std.zig.Tokenizer.init(src); while (true) { const t = tz.next(); if (t.tag == .eof) break; if (t.tag == .invalid) return .{ .invalid = 1 + std.mem.count(u8, src[0..t.loc.start], "\n") }; try toks.append(a, .{ .tag = t.tag, .start = t.loc.start, .end = t.loc.end }); } return .{ .ok = toks.items }; } /// What an identifier token is: a `use` of a name; a `declaration` (after /// `const`, `var` or `fn`, before a `:` outside a container's own level, or in /// a capture's `|...|`); or a `field`, a nested container's member (a field, an /// enum, union or error set member, or the container's own `const`, `var` or /// `fn`). A `field` may share a top-level name (`pub const kept_open = /// &host_file.kept_open;`) and is never that declaration. pub const Role = enum { use, declaration, field }; pub const Ident = struct { tok: usize, start: usize, end: usize, role: Role }; /// Every `.identifier` token not right after `.`, with its role. `zig_rename` /// and `zig_move` both read identifiers only through this. Zig forbids a local /// or parameter shadowing a top-level name, so a matching use or declaration is /// that declaration's. `@"x"` is its own bytes. Two known false declarations /// are safe, since a rename then stops with nothing written: `n` in /// `buf[0..n :0]`, and `(a) | b | c` read as a capture. pub fn identifiers(a: std.mem.Allocator, ts: []const Tok) error{OutOfMemory}![]const Ident { const Opens = enum { block, container, members }; const Brace = struct { kind: Opens, parens: usize }; var out: std.ArrayList(Ident) = .empty; var braces: std.ArrayList(Brace) = .empty; // What the next `{` opens: a container after `struct` or `opaque`; // members after `enum`, `union` or `error` (through `(enum)`, `(u8)`). var next_brace: Opens = .block; var parens: usize = 0; var in_capture = false; for (ts, 0..) |t, i| { const prev: ?Tag = if (i > 0) ts[i - 1].tag else null; const next: ?Tag = if (i + 1 < ts.len) ts[i + 1].tag else null; switch (t.tag) { .keyword_struct, .keyword_opaque => next_brace = .container, .keyword_enum, .keyword_union, .keyword_error => next_brace = .members, .l_paren => parens += 1, .r_paren => parens -|= 1, .doc_comment, .container_doc_comment => {}, .l_brace => { try braces.append(a, .{ .kind = next_brace, .parens = parens }); next_brace = .block; }, .r_brace => { _ = braces.pop(); next_brace = .block; }, .pipe => { if (in_capture) { in_capture = false; } else if (prev != null and (prev.? == .r_paren or prev.? == .keyword_else or prev.? == .keyword_catch or prev.? == .equal_angle_bracket_right) and isCapture(ts[i + 1 ..])) { in_capture = true; } next_brace = .block; }, .identifier => if (prev != .period) { // The file's root is a container. const top: Brace = if (braces.items.len > 0) braces.items[braces.items.len - 1] else .{ .kind = .container, .parens = 0 }; const level = top.kind != .block and parens == top.parens; const member_start = prev == null or switch (prev.?) { .l_brace, .comma, .doc_comment, .container_doc_comment, .semicolon, .r_brace, .keyword_comptime => true, else => false, }; const field = level and member_start and (next == .colon or (top.kind == .members and (next == .comma or next == .r_brace or next == .equal))); // `const` qualifying a pointer (`[]const T`, `*align(4) const T`) // does not declare. const pointer_const = prev == .keyword_const and i >= 2 and switch (ts[i - 2].tag) { .r_bracket, .asterisk, .r_paren, .keyword_allowzero, .keyword_volatile => true, else => false, }; const keyword = (prev == .keyword_const and !pointer_const) or prev == .keyword_var or prev == .keyword_fn; // A nested container's own declaration is its member. const member_decl = keyword and level and braces.items.len > 0; const role: Role = if (field or member_decl) .field else if ((prev == .keyword_const and !pointer_const) or prev == .keyword_var or prev == .keyword_fn or next == .colon or in_capture) .declaration else .use; try out.append(a, .{ .tok = i, .start = t.start, .end = t.end, .role = role }); }, else => next_brace = .block, } } return out.items; } /// Whether the tokens after a `|` are a capture's: `[*]name(, [*]name)*|`. fn isCapture(ts: []const Tok) bool { var i: usize = 0; while (true) { if (i < ts.len and ts[i].tag == .asterisk) i += 1; if (i >= ts.len or ts[i].tag != .identifier) return false; i += 1; if (i < ts.len and ts[i].tag == .pipe) return true; if (i >= ts.len or ts[i].tag != .comma) return false; i += 1; } }

name: repos:shale/src/script/ast.zig
html: //! The tree a script parses to. Every node has its line and column, every //! name is already resolved to a slot in its function's frame, and every call //! names a builtin or a function by index. All of it lives in the run's arena. const std = @import("std"); pub const Pos = struct { line: u32, column: u32 }; pub const Builtin = enum { // the store ls, stat, exists, is_dir, read, read_or, read_lines, line_at, grep, count_lines, count_in, find_in, replace, append, mkdir, remove, remove_tree, walk, edit, // strings split, join, starts_with, ends_with, contains, find, sub, bad_utf8, trim, trim_start, trim_end, upper, lower, tostring, tonumber, parse_int, lines, words, like, rep, substitute, path, match_path, basename, is_name, strip_suffix, between, // regular expressions re_find, re_match, re_replace, re_find_all, // numbers min, max, abs, // dates and formatting date, seconds, human, pad, table, // lists and maps push, pop, sort, keys, has_key, get, count, reverse, take, last, same, // the host now, arg, fail, host, budget, call_bytes, yield, print, }; /// `eq_nil` and `ne_nil` are `==` and `~=` with the literal `nil` on one /// side: the one comparison a map or a list may be in, so `if m == nil` /// reads as written. pub const BinOp = enum { add, sub, mul, idiv, mod, concat, eq, ne, eq_nil, ne_nil, lt, le, gt, ge, @"and", @"or" }; pub const UnOp = enum { neg, not, len }; pub const Expr = struct { pos: Pos, kind: Kind, pub const Kind = union(enum) { nil, boolean: bool, int: i64, string: []const u8, /// A slot in the current function's frame. local: u16, /// A top-level `const`, read in a function: an index into the /// run's constants (`Program.const_names`). constant: u16, index: struct { obj: *Expr, key: *Expr }, call: Call, binary: struct { op: BinOp, left: *Expr, right: *Expr }, unary: struct { op: UnOp, operand: *Expr }, list: []*Expr, map: []MapEntry, empty_table, }; }; pub const MapEntry = struct { key: []const u8, value: *Expr, pos: Pos }; pub const Call = struct { target: Target, args: []*Expr, pub const Target = union(enum) { builtin: Builtin, /// An index into `Program.functions`, set as the call is parsed: a /// function is called only after it is declared. function: u32, /// `attempt(f, ...)`: the function `f`, an index as in `function`, /// called with the rest of the arguments; its error becomes a value. attempt: u32, }; }; pub const Stmt = struct { pos: Pos, kind: Kind, pub const Kind = union(enum) { local: struct { slot: u16, value: ?*Expr }, /// `const NAME = e` at the top level: the script's own slot, and the /// index of the constant that functions declared after it read. constant: struct { slot: u16, index: u16, value: *Expr }, assign: struct { target: *Expr, value: *Expr }, call: *Expr, @"if": struct { arms: []Arm, otherwise: ?[]Stmt }, @"while": struct { cond: *Expr, body: []Stmt }, numeric_for: struct { slot: u16, from: *Expr, to: *Expr, step: ?*Expr, body: []Stmt }, list_for: struct { slot: u16, list: *Expr, body: []Stmt }, @"return": ?*Expr, @"break", @"continue", do: []Stmt, }; }; pub const Arm = struct { cond: *Expr, body: []Stmt }; pub const Function = struct { name: []const u8, pos: Pos, params: u16, /// How many of the last `params` may be left out (`b?`). The parse passes /// nil for each one a call leaves out. optional: u16 = 0, /// Slots in its frame: parameters first, then every local it declares. frame: u16, body: []Stmt, }; pub const Program = struct { /// The script's functions and the prelude functions it calls, in the /// order the parse met them. functions: []Function, /// The top-level `const`s, in order, by name. const_names: []const []const u8 = &.{}, /// The script's own top level, a function with no parameters. main: Function, /// The names its `arg("NAME", ...)` calls read, each once; null when /// one names it by a value other than a string literal, so which names /// it reads cannot be said before it runs (`unreadArg`). args_read: ?[]const []const u8 = &.{}, }; /// **A VALUE GIVEN THAT NOTHING READS** (2026-10-25: `cwd=` given to a /// recipe that reads `dir=` was taken without a word, and the command ran /// in the wrong folder): the first of `given` that no `arg` call of /// `program` names, or null. Null too when the program names one by a /// value, which cannot be checked before it runs. pub fn unreadArg(program: *const Program, given: anytype) ?[]const u8 { const read = program.args_read orelse return null; outer: for (given) |g| { for (read) |r| if (std.mem.eql(u8, r, g.name)) continue :outer; return g.name; } return null; }

name: repos:shale/src/shale_tokens_test.zig
html: //! Tests `shale_tokens`: a Shale file's tokens by the language's own lexer. const std = @import("std"); const testing = std.testing; const T = @import("shale_test_host.zig").T; const host_linux = @import("shale_host_linux.zig"); fn init(t: *T) !void { try t.init(); t.preludes = &.{host_linux.linux_prelude}; } /// A script printing each token of `k.shale`, by `tag`, `line` and `text`. const rows = "for k in shale_tokens(\"k.shale\") do print(k.tag, k.line, k.text) end"; test "shale_tokens: a file's tokens in order, `{tag, text, line, start, stop}`, comments among them; a keyword inside a name is a name; `read(p, start, stop - start)` is the token" { var t: T = undefined; try init(&t); defer t.deinit(); try t.put("k.shale", "-- a\nlocal end_col = 12 + 'x'\n"); try t.expectOutput(rows, "comment\t1\t-- a\nkw_local\t2\tlocal\nname\t2\tend_col\nassign\t2\t=\nint\t2\t12\nplus\t2\t+\nstring\t2\t'x'\n"); try t.expectOutput("for k in shale_tokens(\"k.shale\") do print(k.start, k.stop, read(\"k.shale\", k.start, k.stop - k.start) == k.text) end", "0\t4\ttrue\n5\t10\ttrue\n11\t18\ttrue\n19\t20\ttrue\n21\t23\ttrue\n24\t25\ttrue\n26\t29\ttrue\n"); } test "shale_tokens: `text` is the source's bytes: a string's quotes and escapes as written, a long string's opener and closer, and the newline after its opener" { var t: T = undefined; try init(&t); defer t.deinit(); try t.put("k.shale", "\"a\\n\" [=[\nb]=]"); try t.expectOutput("for k in shale_tokens(\"k.shale\") do print(#k.text, k.stop - k.start) end", "5\t5\n8\t8\n"); try t.expectOutput("print(shale_tokens(\"k.shale\")[1].text == \"\\\"a\\\\n\\\"\", shale_tokens(\"k.shale\")[2].text == \"[=[\\nb]=]\")", "true\ttrue\n"); } test "shale_tokens: a comment's and a string's words are no tokens, a block comment and a long string span their lines, `--[=x` is a line comment, and a line comment leaves its newline and keeps a CR" { var t: T = undefined; try init(&t); defer t.deinit(); try t.put("k.shale", "--[=[ end\nif ]=] x --[=x then\ny = \"-- no\" -- z\r\nw = [==[ ]=] -- ]==] v"); try t.expectOutput(rows, "comment\t1\t--[=[ end\nif ]=]\nname\t2\tx\ncomment\t2\t--[=x then\nname\t3\ty\nassign\t3\t=\nstring\t3\t\"-- no\"\ncomment\t3\t-- z\r\nname\t4\tw\nassign\t4\t=\nstring\t4\t[==[ ]=] -- ]==]\nname\t4\tv\n"); } test "shale_tokens: a file of no tokens, an empty one or one of space, lists none; a file of one comment lists it, with no newline after it" { var t: T = undefined; try init(&t); defer t.deinit(); try t.put("empty.shale", ""); try t.put("space.shale", " \n\t\r\n"); try t.put("k.shale", "--"); try t.expectOutput("print(#shale_tokens(\"empty.shale\"), #shale_tokens(\"space.shale\"))", "0\t0\n"); try t.expectOutput(rows, "comment\t1\t--\n"); } test "shale_tokens: `{tag = ...}` keeps one kind, a keyword or a comment, and none when the file holds none; a tag that is no token's stops, as does the end's, a bad key, and a tag or options of the wrong type" { var t: T = undefined; try init(&t); defer t.deinit(); try t.put("k.shale", "-- a\nif b then c() end -- d\n"); try t.expectOutput("for k in shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {tag = \"comment\"}) do print(k.text, k.line) end", "-- a\t1\n-- d\t2\n"); try t.expectOutput("for k in shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {tag = \"kw_end\"}) do print(k.text, k.start) end", "end\t19\n"); try t.expectOutput("print(#shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {tag = \"string\"}))", "0\n"); try t.expectOutput("print(#shale_tokens(\"k.shale\"))", "9\n"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {tag = \"nope\"})", .atomic, .argument, "no token tag `nope`"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {tag = \"eof\"})", .atomic, .argument, "no token tag `eof`"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {kind = \"name\"})", .atomic, .argument, "takes `tag`, not `kind`"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {tag = 1})", .atomic, .type, "`tag` is a tag's name"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", {\"name\"})", .atomic, .type, "options are a map, not a list"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"k.shale\", 1)", .atomic, .type, "options are a map"); } test "shale_tokens: a file that doesn't lex stops with the lexer's line and message, an unclosed comment as much as a refused construct; a missing file stops too, and a file that lexes but doesn't parse is listed" { var t: T = undefined; try init(&t); defer t.deinit(); try t.put("float.shale", "a\nb = 1.5\n"); try t.put("comment.shale", "a\n\n--[=[ b"); try t.put("nolevel.shale", "--[[ a ]]"); try t.put("parses_not.shale", "end end ("); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"float.shale\")", .atomic, .argument, "float.shale does not lex as Shale at line 2: float literals"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"comment.shale\")", .atomic, .argument, "at line 3: a long comment with no `]=]`"); try t.expectStop("shale_tokens(\"nolevel.shale\")", .atomic, .argument, "a long comment needs a level"); try t.expectOutput("print(#shale_tokens(\"parses_not.shale\"))", "3\n"); var r = t.run("shale_tokens(\"absent.shale\")", .atomic); defer r.deinit(); try testing.expect(r.stop != null); } test "shale_tokens: a step a token, kept or not, more for a file four times the size; `host` takes a path and options, no more or fewer" { var t: T = undefined; try init(&t); defer t.deinit(); const a = t.arena.allocator(); var steps: [2]u64 = undefined; for ([_]usize{ 25, 100 }, 0..) |n, k| { var src: std.ArrayList(u8) = .empty; for (0..n) |_| try src.appendSlice(a, "x = 1\n"); try t.put("n.shale", src.items); var r = t.run("local d = shale_tokens(\"n.shale\", {tag = \"string\"})", .atomic); defer r.deinit(); try testing.expect(r.stop == null); steps[k] = r.steps; } // Three tokens a line: 75 lines more are 225 more. try testing.expect(steps[1] >= steps[0] + 225); try t.expectStop("host(\"shale_tokens\")", .atomic, .argument, "takes a path and options, given 0"); try t.expectStop("host(\"shale_tokens\", \"k\", {}, 1)", .atomic, .argument, "takes a path and options, given 3"); }

name: repos:shale/src/shale_job_record.zig
html: //! A job's record, `<log>.job`: `key=value` lines its reaper writes and every //! later `shale` reads to find the job again. Plain text, no system call, so //! it is the part of jobs a port keeps; the processes it names are //! `shale_jobs.zig`'s. const std = @import("std"); /// A job's record, as `<log>.job` holds it. pub const Record = struct { /// The job's leader. pid: i32 = 0, /// The job's process group, which is its session's. pgid: i32 = 0, /// The leader's start time, raw from `/proc/<pid>/stat`. start: []const u8 = "", /// When the job started, in Unix seconds. started: i64 = 0, /// The job's argv joined by spaces, for display. argv: []const u8 = "", /// The reaper's pid. reaper: i32 = 0, /// The reaper's start time, raw from `/proc/<pid>/stat`. reaper_start: []const u8 = "", /// The exit code, once the job exited. exit: ?u8 = null, /// The signal that ended the job, once it did. signal: ?u32 = null, /// When the job ended, in Unix seconds. ended: ?i64 = null, pub fn done(r: Record) bool { return r.exit != null or r.signal != null; } }; /// Parses a record's text. Returns `null` if it is not a record: a key /// missing (`formatRecord` writes each of the first seven), one it does not /// know or twice, a line that is no `key=value`, or an `argv` escaped /// wrongly. A missing `start` read as "" would make `alive` say false of a /// job that runs. `argv` is unescaped in place, so `text` is changed. pub fn parseRecord(text: []u8) ?Record { var r: Record = .{}; const keys = [_][]const u8{ "pid", "pgid", "start", "started", "argv", "reaper", "reaper_start", "exit", "signal", "ended" }; const required = 7; var seen: [keys.len]bool = @splat(false); var it = std.mem.splitScalar(u8, text, '\n'); while (it.next()) |line_c| { if (line_c.len == 0) continue; // The line, as the part of `text` it is, so `argv` can be unescaped there. const at = @intFromPtr(line_c.ptr) - @intFromPtr(text.ptr); const line = text[at .. at + line_c.len]; const eq = std.mem.indexOfScalar(u8, line, '=') orelse return null; const k = line[0..eq]; const v = line[eq + 1 ..]; const i = for (keys, 0..) |name, i| { if (std.mem.eql(u8, k, name)) break i; } else return null; if (seen[i]) return null; seen[i] = true; switch (i) { 0 => r.pid = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, v, 10) catch return null, 1 => r.pgid = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, v, 10) catch return null, 2 => r.start = v, 3 => r.started = std.fmt.parseInt(i64, v, 10) catch return null, 4 => r.argv = unescape(v) orelse return null, 5 => r.reaper = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, v, 10) catch return null, 6 => r.reaper_start = v, 7 => r.exit = std.fmt.parseInt(u8, v, 10) catch return null, 8 => r.signal = std.fmt.parseInt(u32, v, 10) catch return null, else => r.ended = std.fmt.parseInt(i64, v, 10) catch return null, } } for (seen[0..required]) |s| if (!s) return null; if (r.pid <= 0 or r.pgid <= 0) return null; return r; } /// `argv` as `formatRecord` escapes it: `\n` a newline, `\\` a backslash, /// so no argument starts a line of its own. fn unescape(v: []u8) ?[]u8 { var o: usize = 0; var i: usize = 0; while (i < v.len) : (i += 1) { if (v[i] == '\\') { i += 1; if (i == v.len) return null; v[o] = switch (v[i]) { 'n' => '\n', '\\' => '\\', else => return null, }; } else v[o] = v[i]; o += 1; } return v[0..o]; } /// The record's text in `buf`, `argv` escaped; null if it does not fit, /// never a record cut short. pub fn formatRecord(buf: []u8, r: Record) ?[]u8 { var w: std.Io.Writer = .fixed(buf); w.print("pid={d}\npgid={d}\nstart={s}\nstarted={d}\nargv=", .{ r.pid, r.pgid, r.start, r.started }) catch return null; for (r.argv) |c| switch (c) { '\\' => w.writeAll("\\\\") catch return null, '\n' => w.writeAll("\\n") catch return null, else => w.writeByte(c) catch return null, }; w.print("\nreaper={d}\nreaper_start={s}\n", .{ r.reaper, r.reaper_start }) catch return null; if (r.exit) |c| w.print("exit={d}\n", .{c}) catch return null; if (r.signal) |s| w.print("signal={d}\n", .{s}) catch return null; if (r.ended) |e| w.print("ended={d}\n", .{e}) catch return null; return w.buffered(); } /// The most bytes a job's argv may take in its record, escaped /// (`formatRecord`): the rest of `shale_jobs.zig`'s `writeRecord`'s 8 KiB holds /// the other keys. pub const argv_most = 7168; test "jobs: a record reads back as it was written, and a broken one is none" { var buf: [512]u8 = undefined; const text = formatRecord(&buf, .{ .pid = 42, .pgid = 42, .start = "123", .started = 9, .argv = "zig build", .exit = 3, .ended = 11 }).?; const r = parseRecord(text).?; try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(i32, 42), r.pid); try std.testing.expectEqualStrings("123", r.start); try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(?u8, 3), r.exit); try std.testing.expect(r.done()); try std.testing.expect(parseCopy("pid=x\n") == null); try std.testing.expect(parseCopy("") == null); // A record missing a key, holding one it does not know, or a line that // is no `key=value`, is none: never a record with a key read as empty. try std.testing.expect(parseCopy("pid=42\npgid=42\nstarted=9\nargv=x\nreaper=1\nreaper_start=5\n") == null); try std.testing.expect(parseCopy("pid=42\npgid=42\nstart=1\nstarted=9\nargv=x\nreaper=1\nreaper_start=5\nexitt=3\n") == null); try std.testing.expect(parseCopy("pid=42\npgid=42\nstart=1\nstarted=9\nargv=x\nreaper=1\nreaper_start=5\ngarbage\n") == null); } test "jobs: an argv with a newline or a backslash reads back as it was, and none overrides a key; a key twice is none" { var buf: [512]u8 = undefined; for ([_][]const u8{ "git commit -m one\ntwo", "x\npid=7\nexit=3", "a\\nb \\ c" }) |argv| { const r = parseRecord(formatRecord(&buf, .{ .pid = 42, .pgid = 42, .start = "123", .started = 9, .argv = argv, .reaper = 1, .reaper_start = "5" }).?) orelse return error.TestUnexpectedResult; try std.testing.expectEqualStrings(argv, r.argv); try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(i32, 42), r.pid); try std.testing.expect(!r.done()); } try std.testing.expect(parseCopy("pid=42\npgid=42\nstart=1\nstarted=9\nargv=x\nreaper=1\nreaper_start=5\npid=7\n") == null); try std.testing.expect(parseCopy("pid=42\npgid=42\nstart=1\nstarted=9\nargv=a\\qb\nreaper=1\nreaper_start=5\n") == null); // A record too big for its buffer is none, never one cut short. var small: [64]u8 = undefined; const long: [64]u8 = @splat(120); try std.testing.expect(formatRecord(&small, .{ .pid = 42, .pgid = 42, .start = "123", .started = 9, .argv = &long, .reaper = 1, .reaper_start = "5" }) == null); } /// `parseRecord` of a literal, through a copy it may unescape in place. fn parseCopy(comptime s: []const u8) ?Record { const S = struct { var b: [1024]u8 = undefined; }; @memcpy(S.b[0..s.len], s); return parseRecord(S.b[0..s.len]); }

name: repos:shale/src/script_bench.zig
html: //! Times Shale's hot paths: a few scripts that each lean on one path of the //! interpreter (a loop's iteration, a list's and a map's index, a call, //! building a string), each run on the tree-walker and on the VM as many times //! as fit in about half a second, its time and its steps printed: //! //! zig build script-bench (ReleaseSafe) //! //! Outside the script module: it may name the host. const std = @import("std"); const shale = @import("shale"); const script = shale.script; const cases = [_]struct { name: []const u8, src: []const u8 }{ .{ .name = "a loop's iteration", .src = \\local x = 0 \\for i = 1, 1000000 do x = x + i end \\print(x) }, .{ .name = "a while loop", .src = \\local i = 0 \\while i < 500000 do i = i + 1 end \\print(i) }, .{ .name = "a list, built and indexed", .src = \\local l = {} \\for i = 1, 200000 do push(l, i) end \\local s = 0 \\for i = 1, #l do s = s + l[i] end \\for x in l do s = s + x end \\print(s) }, .{ .name = "a map's fields", .src = \\local m = {a = 1, b = 2, c = 3, size = 4} \\local s = 0 \\for i = 1, 300000 do s = s + m.size + m["a"] end \\print(s) }, .{ .name = "calls", .src = \\function fib(n) \\ if n < 2 then return n end \\ return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2) \\end \\print(fib(22)) }, .{ .name = "a string built by `..`", .src = \\local s = "" \\for i = 1, 5000 do s = s .. "line " .. i .. "\n" end \\print(#s) }, .{ .name = "count_in over 8 MiB", .src = \\print(count_in("bench-8m", "ab")) }, .{ .name = "read 8 MiB whole", .src = \\print(#read("bench-8m")) }, .{ .name = "a string built by join", .src = \\local parts = {} \\for i = 1, 50000 do push(parts, "line " .. i) end \\print(#join(parts, "\n")) }, }; pub fn main(init: std.process.Init) !void { const io = init.io; const gpa = init.gpa; const out = try gpa.alloc(u8, 4096); defer gpa.free(out); var buf: [4096]u8 = undefined; var ow = std.Io.File.stdout().writer(io, &buf); const w = &ow.interface; const budgets: script.Budgets = .{ .steps = 100_000_000, .arena_bytes = 256 * 1024 * 1024, .call_bytes = 64 * 1024 * 1024 }; // The scans' file, in the working folder (the bench's root), removed // after. const big = try gpa.alloc(u8, 8 * 1024 * 1024); defer gpa.free(big); for (big, 0..) |*c, i| c.* = "abc\n"[i % 4]; try std.Io.Dir.cwd().writeFile(io, .{ .sub_path = "bench-8m", .data = big }); defer std.Io.Dir.cwd().deleteFile(io, "bench-8m") catch {}; for (cases) |c| { // The same case on each engine; the tests hold their step counts // equal. var ns_of: [2]f64 = undefined; for ([_]script.Engine{ .walker, .vm }, 0..) |engine, k| { var runs: u64 = 0; var steps: u64 = 0; var arena: usize = 0; const t0 = std.Io.Clock.awake.now(io).nanoseconds; while (runs < 3 or std.Io.Clock.awake.now(io).nanoseconds - t0 < std.time.ns_per_s / 2) : (runs += 1) { var r = script.runOn(engine, io, gpa, ".", c.src, budgets, 0, out, .{}); defer r.deinit(); if (r.stop) |s| { try w.print("{s}: stopped {d}:{d}: {s}\n", .{ c.name, s.line, s.column, s.message }); break; } steps = r.steps; arena = r.arena_bytes; } const ns: f64 = @floatFromInt(std.Io.Clock.awake.now(io).nanoseconds - t0); const per_run = ns / @as(f64, @floatFromInt(runs)); ns_of[k] = per_run; try w.print("{s:<28} {s:<6} {d:>9.2} ms {d:>10} steps {d:>6.1} ns a step {d:>8} KiB arena\n", .{ c.name, @tagName(engine), per_run / 1e6, steps, per_run / @as(f64, @floatFromInt(@max(steps, 1))), arena / 1024 }); } try w.print("{s:<28} the VM in {d:.2}x the walker's time\n", .{ "", ns_of[1] / ns_of[0] }); try w.flush(); } }

name: book_builder/host/abi.zig
html: //! The seam between the host and the Roc archive (an app built on //! platform/). It declares the app's one entry, `roc_main`, which //! platform/main.roc provides; it exports the platform's one hosted function, //! `read_file` (platform/Host.roc), answered by host/book_folder.zig; and it //! exports the runtime functions the archive calls: the allocator, //! `roc_crashed`, `roc_dbg` and `roc_expect_failed`. //! //! Roc lays a record out by alignment, then by field name, so the fields //! below are in that order, not the source's. A tag union with no payloads is //! one byte, its tags numbered alphabetically. host/abi_test.zig holds every //! type here to what `roc glue` makes of the platform //! (host/glue/platform_abi.zig), field by field and tag by tag. //! //! The program makes one Roc call and exits, so everything Roc allocates //! comes from one arena, `allocator`, freed whole when the run ends: //! `roc_dealloc` frees nothing and no refcount is kept by hand. const std = @import("std"); const book_folder = @import("book_folder.zig"); /// A Roc `List(U8)` as glue lays one out: the elements' pointer, the /// length, then the capacity shifted left once (or, for a slice, the /// allocation's pointer with its low bit set). A list the host makes has a /// refcount word just before its bytes. pub const Bytes = extern struct { elements: ?[*]u8, length: usize, capacity_or_alloc_ptr: usize, pub fn slice(b: Bytes) []const u8 { const p = b.elements orelse return ""; return p[0..b.length]; } /// A new list holding a copy of `bytes`, in the run's arena. pub fn from(bytes: []const u8) Bytes { if (bytes.len == 0) return .{ .elements = null, .length = 0, .capacity_or_alloc_ptr = 0 }; const w = @sizeOf(usize); const base = allocate(w + bytes.len, w); std.mem.writeInt(usize, base[0..w], 1, .little); const data = base + w; @memcpy(data[0..bytes.len], bytes); return .{ .elements = data, .length = bytes.len, .capacity_or_alloc_ptr = bytes.len << 1 }; } }; /// Host.roc's `read_file!` answer: the list, then the tag. pub const ReadRec = extern struct { bytes: Bytes, status: book_folder.ReadStatus }; /// platform/main.roc's `main_for_host!` outcome, alphabetical. pub const Outcome = enum(u8) { failed, printed }; /// platform/main.roc's `main_for_host!` answer: the list, then the tag. pub const MainAnswer = extern struct { text: Bytes, outcome: Outcome }; pub extern fn roc_main(folder: Bytes) callconv(.c) MainAnswer; /// What a Roc call may use, set before `roc_main` by `begin`: the arena it /// allocates from and the book it reads. pub var allocator: ?std.mem.Allocator = null; pub var book: ?book_folder.BookFolder = null; pub fn begin(arena: std.mem.Allocator, folder: book_folder.BookFolder) void { allocator = arena; book = folder; } pub export fn read_file(path: Bytes) callconv(.c) ReadRec { const folder = book orelse @panic("read_file: the Roc ran before `begin` named the book"); return switch (folder.read_file(run_arena(), path.slice())) { .found => |bytes| .{ .bytes = .from(bytes), .status = .found }, .not_a_file => .{ .bytes = .from(""), .status = .not_a_file }, .not_found => .{ .bytes = .from(""), .status = .not_found }, .outside_the_book => .{ .bytes = .from(""), .status = .outside_the_book }, .read_failed => .{ .bytes = .from(""), .status = .read_failed }, }; } // The runtime. comptime { @export(&roc_alloc, .{ .name = "roc_alloc" }); @export(&roc_realloc, .{ .name = "roc_realloc" }); @export(&roc_dealloc, .{ .name = "roc_dealloc" }); @export(&roc_crashed, .{ .name = "roc_crashed" }); @export(&roc_dbg, .{ .name = "roc_dbg" }); @export(&roc_expect_failed, .{ .name = "roc_expect_failed" }); } fn run_arena() std.mem.Allocator { return allocator orelse @panic("roc_alloc: the Roc ran before `begin` gave it an arena"); } /// Each allocation's length sits in a header before what Roc is given, so /// `roc_realloc`, which is not told it, knows how much to copy. The header /// is 16 bytes because Roc asks for at most 16's alignment. const header = 16; fn allocate(len: usize, alignment: usize) [*]u8 { if (alignment > header) std.debug.panic("roc_alloc: an alignment of {d}, past the header's {d}", .{ alignment, header }); const got = run_arena().alignedAlloc(u8, .fromByteUnits(header), header + len) catch std.debug.panic("roc_alloc: out of memory ({d} bytes)", .{len}); std.mem.writeInt(usize, got[0..@sizeOf(usize)], len, .little); return got.ptr + header; } fn roc_alloc(len: usize, alignment: usize) callconv(.c) *anyopaque { return allocate(len, alignment); } fn roc_realloc(ptr: *anyopaque, len: usize, alignment: usize) callconv(.c) *anyopaque { const old: [*]u8 = @ptrCast(ptr); const was = std.mem.readInt(usize, (old - header)[0..@sizeOf(usize)], .little); const new = allocate(len, alignment); @memcpy(new[0..@min(was, len)], old[0..@min(was, len)]); return new; } fn roc_dealloc(ptr: *anyopaque, alignment: usize) callconv(.c) void { _ = ptr; _ = alignment; } fn roc_crashed(bytes: [*]const u8, len: usize) callconv(.c) void { std.debug.panic("roc crashed: {s}", .{bytes[0..len]}); } fn roc_dbg(bytes: [*]const u8, len: usize) callconv(.c) void { std.debug.print("roc dbg: {s}\n", .{bytes[0..len]}); } fn roc_expect_failed(bytes: [*]const u8, len: usize) callconv(.c) void { std.debug.panic("roc: an inline expect failed: {s}", .{bytes[0..len]}); }

name: book_builder/host/abi_test.zig
html: //! Holds host/abi.zig to roc glue's layout of the platform, at compile time. //! Each C function glue declares for the platform (the app's entries) is //! held to abi.zig's function of that symbol, argument by argument and the //! answer: a record field by field by name (its offset, and what it holds, //! down through records, unions and lists), a list by its element, a tag //! union's tags by number, a number by its type. Two same-sized fields //! swapped pass a size check and fail here, naming the function, the field //! and both offsets. A function either side has and the other has not //! fails the build. glue/platform_abi.zig is glue's output, regenerated by //! `shale book_builder/tools/glue.shale` after a change to platform/. //! //! The checker is roc-screensaver's `host/abi_test.zig`, copied on purpose //! and allowed to drift: each platform holds its own seam. const std = @import("std"); const abi = @import("abi.zig"); const glue = @import("glue/platform_abi.zig"); /// The runtime's functions, which the host exports and glue declares as the /// host's to give; they are not part of the platform's own seam. const runtime = [_][]const u8{ "roc_alloc", "roc_dealloc", "roc_realloc", "roc_dbg", "roc_expect_failed", "roc_crashed" }; /// The seam's symbols in `M`: each `pub` C function but the runtime's. fn seamNames(comptime M: type) []const []const u8 { comptime { @setEvalBranchQuota(200_000); var names: []const []const u8 = &.{}; for (@typeInfo(M).@"struct".decl_names) |n| { const T = @TypeOf(@field(M, n)); if (@typeInfo(T) != .@"fn") continue; if (@typeInfo(T).@"fn".attrs.@"callconv".eql(.c) and !has(&runtime, n)) names = names ++ &[_][]const u8{n}; } return names; } } const glue_names = seamNames(glue); const abi_names = seamNames(abi); fn has(comptime names: []const []const u8, comptime name: []const u8) bool { for (names) |n| if (std.mem.eql(u8, n, name)) return true; return false; } /// Why abi.zig's `Want` is not laid out as roc glue's `Got`, at `at` (a path /// from the function: `.field`, `[]` for a list's element), or null when /// they agree. fn mismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { @setEvalBranchQuota(1_000_000); return switch (@typeInfo(Got)) { .@"struct" => if (@hasField(Got, "elements_ptr")) listMismatch(Want, Got, at) else recordMismatch(Want, Got, at), .@"union" => unionMismatch(Want, Got, at), .@"enum" => tagsMismatch(Want, Got, at), else => if (Want == Got) null else at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in abi.zig, " ++ @typeName(Got) ++ " in roc glue", }; } /// A Roc list as abi.zig lays one out: an extern struct of three words, the /// elements' pointer, the length and the capacity. fn isList(comptime T: type) bool { const info = @typeInfo(T); if (info != .@"struct" or info.@"struct".layout != .@"extern") return false; const s = info.@"struct"; if (s.field_names.len != 3) return false; const P = s.field_types[0]; if (@typeInfo(P) != .optional or @typeInfo(@typeInfo(P).optional.child) != .pointer) return false; return std.mem.eql(u8, s.field_names[1], "length") and s.field_types[1] == usize and std.mem.eql(u8, s.field_names[2], "capacity_or_alloc_ptr") and s.field_types[2] == usize; } fn elementOf(comptime L: type) type { return @typeInfo(@typeInfo(@typeInfo(L).@"struct".field_types[0]).optional.child).pointer.child; } fn listMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { if (!isList(Want)) return at ++ ": a List in roc glue, " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in abi.zig"; if (@sizeOf(Want) != @sizeOf(Got) or @offsetOf(Want, "length") != @offsetOf(Got, "length") or @offsetOf(Want, "capacity_or_alloc_ptr") != @offsetOf(Got, "capacity_or_alloc_ptr")) return at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " is no list as roc glue lays one out"; return mismatch(elementOf(Want), elementOf(Got), at ++ "[]"); } fn recordMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { const info = @typeInfo(Want); if (info != .@"struct" or info.@"struct".layout != .@"extern") return at ++ ": a record in roc glue, " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in abi.zig, no extern struct"; const got = @typeInfo(Got).@"struct"; for (got.field_names, got.field_types) |name, G| { const here = at ++ "." ++ name; if (!@hasField(Want, name)) return here ++ ": in roc glue, not in " ++ @typeName(Want); if (@offsetOf(Want, name) != @offsetOf(Got, name)) return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: at byte {d} of {s}, at byte {d} in roc glue", .{ here, @offsetOf(Want, name), @typeName(Want), @offsetOf(Got, name) }, ); if (mismatch(@FieldType(Want, name), G, here)) |m| return m; } for (info.@"struct".field_names) |name| { if (!@hasField(Got, name)) return at ++ "." ++ name ++ ": in " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ ", not in roc glue"; } return sizeMismatch(Want, Got, at); } /// A tag union's payload: every member by name, each at offset 0. fn unionMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { const info = @typeInfo(Want); if (info != .@"union" or info.@"union".layout != .@"extern") return at ++ ": a payload union in roc glue, " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in abi.zig, no extern union"; const got = @typeInfo(Got).@"union"; for (got.field_names, got.field_types) |name, G| { if (!@hasField(Want, name)) return at ++ "." ++ name ++ ": in roc glue, not in " ++ @typeName(Want); if (mismatch(@FieldType(Want, name), G, at ++ "." ++ name)) |m| return m; } if (info.@"union".field_names.len != got.field_names.len) return at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " has members roc glue has not"; return sizeMismatch(Want, Got, at); } fn sizeMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { if (@sizeOf(Want) == @sizeOf(Got) and @alignOf(Want) == @alignOf(Got)) return null; return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: {s} is {d} bytes aligned to {d}, roc glue's {d} aligned to {d}", .{ at, @typeName(Want), @sizeOf(Want), @alignOf(Want), @sizeOf(Got), @alignOf(Got) }, ); } /// The tag of `Want` that is Roc's tag `glue_name`, the names matched /// without case or underscores. fn tagNamed(comptime Want: type, comptime glue_name: []const u8) ?[:0]const u8 { for (@typeInfo(Want).@"enum".field_names) |name| { if (std.mem.eql(u8, bare(name), bare(glue_name))) return name; } return null; } fn bare(comptime name: []const u8) []const u8 { var out: []const u8 = ""; for (name) |c| { if (c != '_') out = out ++ &[_]u8{std.ascii.toLower(c)}; } return out; } fn tagsMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { if (@typeInfo(Want) != .@"enum") return at ++ ": tags in roc glue, " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in abi.zig"; if (@sizeOf(Want) != @sizeOf(Got)) return at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " is not roc glue's size"; const got = @typeInfo(Got).@"enum"; for (got.field_names, got.field_values) |glue_name, value| { const name = tagNamed(Want, glue_name) orelse return at ++ ": the tag `" ++ glue_name ++ "` is roc glue's, not " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ "'s"; if (@backingInt(@field(Want, name)) != value) return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: the tag `{s}` is {d} in {s}, {d} in roc glue", .{ at, name, @backingInt(@field(Want, name)), @typeName(Want), value }, ); } if (@typeInfo(Want).@"enum".field_names.len != got.field_names.len) return at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " has tags roc glue has not"; return null; } /// Symbol `name`'s two declarations, argument by argument, then the answer. fn fnMismatch(comptime name: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { if (!@hasDecl(abi, name)) return name ++ ": roc glue declares it, abi.zig has no `pub` function of the name"; const want = @typeInfo(@TypeOf(@field(abi, name))).@"fn"; const got = @typeInfo(@TypeOf(@field(glue, name))).@"fn"; if (want.param_types.len != got.param_types.len) return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: {d} arguments in abi.zig, {d} in roc glue", .{ name, want.param_types.len, got.param_types.len }, ); for (want.param_types, got.param_types, 0..) |W, G, i| { if (mismatch(W.?, G.?, std.fmt.comptimePrint("{s} argument {d}", .{ name, i }))) |m| return m; } return mismatch(want.return_type.?, got.return_type.?, name ++ "'s answer"); } comptime { @setEvalBranchQuota(1_000_000); for (abi_names) |n| { if (!has(glue_names, n)) @compileError(n ++ ": abi.zig has it, the roc glue snapshot has not; regenerate it: shale book_builder/tools/glue.shale"); } for (glue_names) |n| { if (fnMismatch(n)) |m| @compileError("roc glue lays the seam out unlike abi.zig: " ++ m); } } fn contains(haystack: []const u8, needle: []const u8) bool { return std.mem.indexOf(u8, haystack, needle) != null; } test "roc glue declares every function abi.zig has, and no other: roc_main and read_file" { try std.testing.expectEqual(abi_names.len, glue_names.len); try std.testing.expectEqual(2, abi_names.len); try std.testing.expect(has(abi_names, "roc_main") and has(abi_names, "read_file")); } test "each answer is its list, then its tag byte at 24, in 32 bytes" { try std.testing.expectEqual(32, @sizeOf(abi.ReadRec)); try std.testing.expectEqual(24, @offsetOf(abi.ReadRec, "status")); try std.testing.expectEqual(32, @sizeOf(abi.MainAnswer)); try std.testing.expectEqual(24, @offsetOf(abi.MainAnswer, "outcome")); } test "a renumbered tag, a missing tag and a swapped field each fail the check, named" { // The read's tags in the source's order of thought rather than alphabetically. const Renumbered = enum(u8) { found, not_found, not_a_file, outside_the_book, read_failed }; const t = comptime mismatch(Renumbered, glue.FoundOrNotAFileOrNotFoundOrOutsideTheBookOrReadFailed, "read_file's answer.status").?; try std.testing.expect(contains(t, "the tag `not_a_file` is 2 in ")); // The read's tags without the refusal. const NoRefusal = enum(u8) { found, not_a_file, not_found, read_failed }; const n = comptime mismatch(NoRefusal, glue.FoundOrNotAFileOrNotFoundOrOutsideTheBookOrReadFailed, "status").?; try std.testing.expect(contains(n, "the tag `outside_the_book` is roc glue's")); // The tag before the list: the same fields, the wrong offsets. const Swapped = extern struct { status: @import("book_folder.zig").ReadStatus, bytes: abi.Bytes }; const s = comptime mismatch(Swapped, glue.HostRead_file, "read_file's answer").?; try std.testing.expect(contains(s, "read_file's answer.bytes: at byte 8 of ")); // The layouts abi.zig has pass. try std.testing.expect(comptime mismatch(abi.ReadRec, glue.HostRead_file, "read_file's answer") == null); try std.testing.expect(comptime mismatch(abi.MainAnswer, glue.Main_for_host, "roc_main's answer") == null); }

name: book_builder/host/book_folder.zig
html: //! The book's folder, and the one read the platform allows under it. A path //! the app names is relative to the folder, and nothing outside the folder is //! ever read: `read_file` answers `outside_the_book` for a path that holds a //! NUL byte, starts with `/`, or climbs above the folder with `..`, and for //! one whose file, once opened, turns out to live elsewhere because a //! symbolic link on its way points out of the folder. //! //! The link check is made on the opened file itself (`File.realPath`, which //! asks the kernel where the open descriptor's file is), not on the path, so //! nothing can be swapped in between the check and the read. A link that //! stays inside the folder is followed. //! //! Every answer is a tag, never a crash: the app decides what a missing or //! refused file means for the book. const std = @import("std"); const Io = std.Io; /// The most bytes a read answers; a larger file is `read_failed`, so one /// huge file can't exhaust the build's memory. 16 MiB is far past any /// chapter of a book. pub const read_most = 16 * 1024 * 1024; /// The answer's tags in Roc's order, alphabetical, as they cross the seam /// (host/abi.zig). pub const ReadStatus = enum(u8) { found, not_a_file, not_found, outside_the_book, read_failed }; pub const ReadAnswer = union(ReadStatus) { found: []const u8, not_a_file, not_found, outside_the_book, read_failed, }; /// Whether `path`, by its spelling alone, stays inside the folder: no NUL, /// not absolute, and no `..` that climbs above where it starts. `a/../b` is /// inside; `a/../../b` is not. An empty part and `.` stay where they are. pub fn is_spelled_inside(path: []const u8) bool { if (std.mem.indexOfScalar(u8, path, 0) != null) return false; if (std.mem.startsWith(u8, path, "/")) return false; var depth: usize = 0; var parts = std.mem.splitScalar(u8, path, '/'); while (parts.next()) |part| { if (part.len == 0 or std.mem.eql(u8, part, ".")) continue; if (std.mem.eql(u8, part, "..")) { if (depth == 0) return false; depth -= 1; } else depth += 1; } return true; } /// Whether `real`, a canonical absolute path, is `folder` or below it. The /// byte after the folder's own path must be a `/`, so `/books/a` does not /// hold `/books/ab`. pub fn is_real_path_inside(folder: []const u8, real: []const u8) bool { if (!std.mem.startsWith(u8, real, folder)) return false; if (real.len == folder.len) return true; if (std.mem.eql(u8, folder, "/")) return true; return real[folder.len] == '/'; } pub const BookFolder = struct { io: Io, dir: Io.Dir, /// The folder's canonical absolute path, for the link check. real: []const u8, /// The folder at `path` under `parent`, opened for the run. `real` is /// kept in `arena`. pub fn open(io: Io, arena: std.mem.Allocator, parent: Io.Dir, path: []const u8) !BookFolder { const dir = try parent.openDir(io, path, .{}); errdefer dir.close(io); var buf: [std.fs.max_path_bytes]u8 = undefined; const n = try dir.realPath(io, &buf); return .{ .io = io, .dir = dir, .real = try arena.dupe(u8, buf[0..n]) }; } pub fn close(book: BookFolder) void { book.dir.close(book.io); } /// The file at `path`, relative to the folder: `found` with its bytes in /// `arena`, or the tag that says why not. pub fn read_file(book: BookFolder, arena: std.mem.Allocator, path: []const u8) ReadAnswer { if (!is_spelled_inside(path)) return .outside_the_book; const spelled = if (path.len == 0) "." else path; const file = book.dir.openFile(book.io, spelled, .{}) catch |e| return switch (e) { error.FileNotFound, error.NotDir => .not_found, error.IsDir => .not_a_file, else => .read_failed, }; defer file.close(book.io); var buf: [std.fs.max_path_bytes]u8 = undefined; const n = file.realPath(book.io, &buf) catch return .read_failed; if (!is_real_path_inside(book.real, buf[0..n])) return .outside_the_book; const st = file.stat(book.io) catch return .read_failed; if (st.kind != .file) return .not_a_file; if (st.size > read_most) return .read_failed; const bytes = arena.alloc(u8, @intCast(st.size)) catch return .read_failed; const got = file.readPositionalAll(book.io, bytes, 0) catch return .read_failed; return .{ .found = bytes[0..got] }; } };

name: repos:roc-chat/host/seam_test.zig
html: //! **ROC GLUE HOLDS EVERY SEAM RECORD**: each C function `roc glue` //! declares for the platform (Host.roc's primitives, and the app's five //! entries) is held at compile time to host/seam.zig's function of that //! symbol, argument by argument and the answer: a record field by field by //! name (its offset, and what it holds, down through records and lists), a //! list by its element, a tag union tag by tag by number, a number by its //! type. Two same-sized fields swapped in a hand-laid record pass a size //! assert and fail here, naming the function, the field and both offsets. //! //! **NOTHING IS SKIPPED**: a function either side has and the other has not //! fails the build. glue/platform_abi.zig is glue's output, regenerated by //! `shale tools/glue.shale` after a change to platform/. const std = @import("std"); /// **THE TESTS PLANT FAILURES, AND EACH LOGS A WARNING**: the tests check /// every answer themselves, so only errors are logged while they run. pub const std_options: std.Options = .{ .log_level = .err }; const seam = @import("seam.zig"); const files = @import("file_primitives.zig"); const glue = @import("glue/platform_abi.zig"); /// The runtime's functions, which the host exports and glue declares as /// the host's to give, never part of the platform's own seam. const runtime = [_][]const u8{ "roc_alloc", "roc_dealloc", "roc_realloc", "roc_dbg", "roc_expect_failed", "roc_crashed" }; /// The seam's symbols in `M`: each `pub` C function, but the runtime's. fn seamNames(comptime M: type) []const []const u8 { comptime { @setEvalBranchQuota(200_000); var names: []const []const u8 = &.{}; for (@typeInfo(M).@"struct".decl_names) |n| { const T = @TypeOf(@field(M, n)); if (@typeInfo(T) != .@"fn") continue; if (@typeInfo(T).@"fn".attrs.@"callconv".eql(.c) and !has(&runtime, n)) names = names ++ &[_][]const u8{n}; } return names; } } const glue_names = seamNames(glue); const seam_names = seamNames(seam); fn has(comptime names: []const []const u8, comptime name: []const u8) bool { for (names) |n| if (std.mem.eql(u8, n, name)) return true; return false; } /// Why seam.zig's `Want` is not laid out as roc glue's `Got`, at `at` (a /// path from the function: `.field`, `[]` for a list's element), or null /// when they agree. fn mismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { @setEvalBranchQuota(1_000_000); return switch (@typeInfo(Got)) { .@"struct" => if (@hasField(Got, "elements_ptr")) listMismatch(Want, Got, at) else recordMismatch(Want, Got, at), .@"enum" => tagsMismatch(Want, Got, at), else => if (Want == Got) null else at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in seam.zig, " ++ @typeName(Got) ++ " in roc glue", }; } /// A Roc list as seam.zig lays one out: an extern struct of three words, /// the elements' pointer, the length and the capacity. fn isList(comptime T: type) bool { const info = @typeInfo(T); if (info != .@"struct" or info.@"struct".layout != .@"extern") return false; const s = info.@"struct"; if (s.field_names.len != 3) return false; const P = s.field_types[0]; if (@typeInfo(P) != .optional or @typeInfo(@typeInfo(P).optional.child) != .pointer) return false; return std.mem.eql(u8, s.field_names[1], "length") and s.field_types[1] == usize and std.mem.eql(u8, s.field_names[2], "capacity_or_alloc_ptr") and s.field_types[2] == usize; } fn elementOf(comptime List: type) type { return @typeInfo(@typeInfo(@typeInfo(List).@"struct".field_types[0]).optional.child).pointer.child; } fn listMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { if (!isList(Want)) return at ++ ": a List in roc glue, " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in seam.zig"; if (@sizeOf(Want) != @sizeOf(Got) or @offsetOf(Want, "length") != @offsetOf(Got, "length") or @offsetOf(Want, "capacity_or_alloc_ptr") != @offsetOf(Got, "capacity_or_alloc_ptr")) return at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " is no list as roc glue lays one out"; return mismatch(elementOf(Want), elementOf(Got), at ++ "[]"); } fn recordMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { const info = @typeInfo(Want); if (info != .@"struct" or info.@"struct".layout != .@"extern") return at ++ ": a record in roc glue, " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in seam.zig, no extern struct"; const got = @typeInfo(Got).@"struct"; for (got.field_names, got.field_types) |name, G| { const here = at ++ "." ++ name; if (!@hasField(Want, name)) return here ++ ": in roc glue, not in " ++ @typeName(Want); if (@offsetOf(Want, name) != @offsetOf(Got, name)) return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: at byte {d} of {s}, at byte {d} in roc glue", .{ here, @offsetOf(Want, name), @typeName(Want), @offsetOf(Got, name) }, ); if (mismatch(@FieldType(Want, name), G, here)) |m| return m; } for (info.@"struct".field_names) |name| { if (!@hasField(Got, name)) return at ++ "." ++ name ++ ": in " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ ", not in roc glue"; } if (@sizeOf(Want) != @sizeOf(Got) or @alignOf(Want) != @alignOf(Got)) return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: {s} is {d} bytes aligned to {d}, roc glue's {d} aligned to {d}", .{ at, @typeName(Want), @sizeOf(Want), @alignOf(Want), @sizeOf(Got), @alignOf(Got) }, ); return null; } /// The tag of `Want` that is Roc's tag `glue_name`. **NAMES MATCH WITHOUT /// THEIR UNDERSCORES**: glue snake-cases `NotUtf8` its own way. fn tagNamed(comptime Want: type, comptime glue_name: []const u8) ?[:0]const u8 { for (@typeInfo(Want).@"enum".field_names) |name| { if (std.mem.eql(u8, bare(name), bare(glue_name))) return name; } return null; } fn bare(comptime name: []const u8) []const u8 { var out: []const u8 = ""; for (name) |c| { if (c != '_') out = out ++ &[_]u8{std.ascii.toLower(c)}; } return out; } /// Tag by tag, by number. fn tagsMismatch(comptime Want: type, comptime Got: type, comptime at: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { if (@typeInfo(Want) != .@"enum") return at ++ ": tags in roc glue, " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " in seam.zig"; if (@sizeOf(Want) != @sizeOf(Got)) return at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " is not roc glue's size"; const got = @typeInfo(Got).@"enum"; for (got.field_names, got.field_values) |glue_name, value| { const name = tagNamed(Want, glue_name) orelse return at ++ ": the tag `" ++ glue_name ++ "` is roc glue's, not " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ "'s"; if (@backingInt(@field(Want, name)) != value) return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: the tag `{s}` is {d} in {s}, {d} in roc glue", .{ at, name, @backingInt(@field(Want, name)), @typeName(Want), value }, ); } if (@typeInfo(Want).@"enum".field_names.len != got.field_names.len) return at ++ ": " ++ @typeName(Want) ++ " has tags roc glue has not"; return null; } /// Symbol `name`'s two declarations, argument by argument, then the answer. fn fnMismatch(comptime name: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { if (!@hasDecl(seam, name)) return name ++ ": roc glue declares it, seam.zig has no `pub` function of the name"; const want = @typeInfo(@TypeOf(@field(seam, name))).@"fn"; const got = @typeInfo(@TypeOf(@field(glue, name))).@"fn"; if (want.param_types.len != got.param_types.len) return std.fmt.comptimePrint( "{s}: {d} arguments in seam.zig, {d} in roc glue", .{ name, want.param_types.len, got.param_types.len }, ); for (want.param_types, got.param_types, 0..) |W, G, i| { if (mismatch(W.?, G.?, std.fmt.comptimePrint("{s} argument {d}", .{ name, i }))) |m| return m; } return mismatch(want.return_type.?, got.return_type.?, name ++ "'s answer"); } comptime { @setEvalBranchQuota(1_000_000); for (seam_names) |n| { if (!has(glue_names, n)) @compileError(n ++ ": seam.zig has it, the roc glue snapshot has not; regenerate it: shale tools/glue.shale"); } for (glue_names) |n| { if (fnMismatch(n)) |m| @compileError("roc glue lays the seam out unlike seam.zig: " ++ m); } } fn answerOf(comptime f: anytype) type { return @typeInfo(@TypeOf(f)).@"fn".return_type.?; } fn contains(haystack: []const u8, needle: []const u8) bool { return std.mem.indexOf(u8, haystack, needle) != null; } test "roc glue declares every function seam.zig has, and no other: nineteen primitives and five entries" { try std.testing.expectEqual(seam_names.len, glue_names.len); try std.testing.expectEqual(24, seam_names.len); } test "the password rule `hash-password` asks is the app's: 1 to 72 bytes of UTF-8" { var arena_state = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.init(std.testing.allocator); defer arena_state.deinit(); const a = arena_state.allocator(); seam.begin(.{ .arena = a }); defer seam.end(); for ([_][]const u8{ "hunter2", "x", try repeated(a, "x", 72), try repeated(a, "é", 36) }) |good| { try std.testing.expectEqual(seam.PasswordRule.accepted, seam.roc_password_verdict(.from(good))); } for ([_][]const u8{ "", try repeated(a, "x", 73), try repeated(a, "é", 37), "\xff", "hunter\xc3" }) |bad| { try std.testing.expectEqual(seam.PasswordRule.refused, seam.roc_password_verdict(.from(bad))); } } test "a swap fails the check, naming the function, the field and the offsets" { // The response's first two lists exchanged, the size the same. const Swapped = extern struct { headers: seam.HeaderList, body: seam.RocBytes, stream_holder: seam.RocBytes, stream_key: seam.RocBytes, status: u16, kind: seam.AnswerKind }; const m = comptime mismatch(Swapped, answerOf(glue.roc_handle_http_request), "answer").?; try std.testing.expect(contains(m, "answer.body: at byte 24 of ")); try std.testing.expect(contains(m, "at byte 0 in roc glue")); // Two tags renumbered. const Renumbered = enum(u8) { appended, failed, not_utf8, missing_directory, path_refused }; const t = comptime mismatch(Renumbered, answerOf(glue.append_utf8_bytes_to_file), "answer").?; try std.testing.expect(contains(t, "is 3 in ")); } /// `text`, `n` times over. fn repeated(a: std.mem.Allocator, text: []const u8, n: usize) ![]const u8 { const out = try a.alloc(u8, text.len * n); for (0..n) |i| @memcpy(out[i * text.len ..][0..text.len], text); return out; }

name: repos:zig-webbox/src/log_view.zig
html: //! log_view: the host's log as plain text, for an agent to fetch and grep //! (metal-vmm QUEUE 189.3). Part of the `webbox` library: pure, given the //! log's text and a filter; admin_log.zig serves it. //! //! **PLAIN TEXT, NOT JSON.** The log is text already, and the question an //! agent asks of it is a grep ("what happened at 14:02", "every 503"): plain //! text is `curl | grep` with nothing to undo, where JSON would quote every //! line and add nothing a line does not already say. What the text is comes //! first, in header lines that each begin `# `, so `grep -v '^#'` is the log //! alone. //! //! **THE FILTERS**, each optional, all of them together: //! //! since=2026-10-13T14:02 lines from then on: an ISO UTC time, or any //! leading part of one (`2026-10-13T14`). A //! request's line carries its time (189.2); a //! line without one is taken as of the last time //! before it, and a line before any is left out. //! until=2026-10-13T14:03 lines before then (the same spelling). //! request=12 request 12's line and the lines under it (its //! body's, its upload's: indented four spaces). //! path=/gopher/chat the requests whose path begins so, and the //! lines under them. //! boot=this|before|both this boot's log, the one before it (kept //! across a restart), or both (the default). const std = @import("std"); const http = @import("http.zig"); pub const Boot = enum { both, this, before }; pub const Filter = struct { since: ?[]const u8 = null, until: ?[]const u8 = null, request: ?u64 = null, path: ?[]const u8 = null, boot: Boot = .both, fn any(f: Filter) bool { return f.since != null or f.until != null or f.request != null or f.path != null; } }; /// The filter a request's query asks for. A value spelled wrong is /// `error.BadFilter`, which the page answers 400 with what is allowed; a bad /// `%` escape is `error.MalformedForm`, also the client's. pub fn parseFilter(alloc: std.mem.Allocator, target: []const u8) !Filter { const q = if (std.mem.indexOfScalar(u8, target, '?')) |i| target[i + 1 ..] else ""; var f: Filter = .{}; errdefer if (f.since) |v| alloc.free(v); errdefer if (f.until) |v| alloc.free(v); errdefer if (f.path) |v| alloc.free(v); if (try http.formField(alloc, q, "since")) |v| f.since = try timeOf(alloc, v); if (try http.formField(alloc, q, "until")) |v| f.until = try timeOf(alloc, v); if (try http.formField(alloc, q, "request")) |v| { defer alloc.free(v); // Digits only: no sign, no space, no `_` (std's parseInt takes `+5`). if (v.len == 0) return error.BadFilter; for (v) |c| if (!std.ascii.isDigit(c)) return error.BadFilter; f.request = std.fmt.parseInt(u64, v, 10) catch return error.BadFilter; } if (try http.formField(alloc, q, "path")) |v| { if (v.len == 0 or v[0] != '/') { alloc.free(v); return error.BadFilter; } f.path = v; } if (try http.formField(alloc, q, "boot")) |v| { defer alloc.free(v); f.boot = std.meta.stringToEnum(Boot, v) orelse return error.BadFilter; } return f; } /// The spelling a time is given in: `2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z`, or any /// leading part of it, a year at least. `0` is a digit; the rest is itself. const time_shape = "0000-00-00T00:00:00.000Z"; fn timeOf(alloc: std.mem.Allocator, v: []const u8) ![]const u8 { if (v.len < 4 or v.len > time_shape.len or !shaped(v)) { alloc.free(v); return error.BadFilter; } return v; } fn shaped(v: []const u8) bool { for (v, time_shape[0..v.len]) |c, want| { if (want == '0') { if (!std.ascii.isDigit(c)) return false; } else if (c != want) return false; } return true; } /// The time a line leads with (after its indent), whole, or null. fn timeAt(line: []const u8) ?[]const u8 { const t = std.mem.trimStart(u8, line, " "); if (t.len < time_shape.len or !shaped(t[0..time_shape.len])) return null; return t[0..time_shape.len]; } const RequestLine = struct { number: u64, path: []const u8 }; /// A request's line: `request N: METHOD PATH -> ...`, after its time. fn requestAt(line: []const u8) ?RequestLine { var t = std.mem.trimStart(u8, line, " "); if (timeAt(t) != null) t = t[time_shape.len..]; t = std.mem.trimStart(u8, t, " "); if (!std.mem.startsWith(u8, t, "request ")) return null; t = t["request ".len..]; const colon = std.mem.indexOfScalar(u8, t, ':') orelse return null; // The server's own number, written just now: not a request's to spell. const number = std.fmt.parseInt(u64, t[0..colon], 10) catch return null; var words = std.mem.tokenizeScalar(u8, t[colon + 1 ..], ' '); _ = words.next() orelse return null; // the method const path = words.next() orelse return null; return .{ .number = number, .path = path }; } /// What one boot's text gave: how many lines it held and how many were kept, /// and the time its oldest timed line carries. pub const Counted = struct { lines: usize = 0, kept: usize = 0, oldest: ?[]const u8 = null }; /// Writes the lines of `text` that `f` keeps, each with its newline. pub fn writeLines(w: *std.Io.Writer, text: []const u8, f: Filter) std.Io.Writer.Error!Counted { var c: Counted = .{}; var time: ?[]const u8 = null; var block: ?RequestLine = null; var it = std.mem.splitScalar(u8, text, '\n'); while (it.next()) |line| { if (line.len == 0 and it.index == null) break; // the text's last newline c.lines += 1; if (timeAt(line)) |t| { time = t; if (c.oldest == null) c.oldest = t; } if (requestAt(line)) |r| { block = r; } else if (!std.mem.startsWith(u8, line, " ")) block = null; if (!keeps(f, time, block)) continue; c.kept += 1; try w.writeAll(line); try w.writeByte('\n'); } return c; } fn keeps(f: Filter, time: ?[]const u8, block: ?RequestLine) bool { if (f.since) |since| { const t = time orelse return false; if (std.mem.order(u8, t, since) == .lt) return false; } if (f.until) |until| { const t = time orelse return false; if (std.mem.order(u8, t, until) != .lt) return false; } if (f.request) |n| { const b = block orelse return false; if (b.number != n) return false; } if (f.path) |p| { const b = block orelse return false; if (!std.mem.startsWith(u8, b.path, p)) return false; } return true; } const testing = std.testing; const sample = " boot: ram 1 GiB\n" ++ " 2026-10-13T14:01:59.900Z request 11: GET /gopher/chat -> ok, 200 in 3.0 ms (base: 1)\n" ++ " 2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z request 12: POST /gopher/chat/c/1_2/T/upload -> ok, 200 in 41.3 ms (base: 2)\n" ++ " upload: 9000 bytes, arrived in 40 ms\n" ++ " stream ended: displaced\n" ++ " 2026-10-13T14:03:00.000Z request 13: GET /admin/host -> ok, 200 in 9.1 ms (base: 3)\n"; fn kept(f: Filter) ![]const u8 { var buf: [2048]u8 = undefined; var w: std.Io.Writer = .fixed(&buf); _ = try writeLines(&w, sample, f); return testing.allocator.dupe(u8, w.buffered()); } fn expectKept(f: Filter, want: []const u8) !void { const got = try kept(f); defer testing.allocator.free(got); try testing.expectEqualStrings(want, got); } test "log view: no filter keeps every line, and counts them, the oldest time among them" { var buf: [2048]u8 = undefined; var w: std.Io.Writer = .fixed(&buf); const c = try writeLines(&w, sample, .{}); try testing.expectEqualStrings(sample, w.buffered()); try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 6), c.lines); try testing.expectEqual(@as(usize, 6), c.kept); try testing.expectEqualStrings("2026-10-13T14:01:59.900Z", c.oldest.?); } test "log view: since and until by any leading part of a time, a line without one as of the time before it" { try expectKept(.{ .since = "2026-10-13T14:02" }, \\ 2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z request 12: POST /gopher/chat/c/1_2/T/upload -> ok, 200 in 41.3 ms (base: 2) \\ upload: 9000 bytes, arrived in 40 ms \\ stream ended: displaced \\ 2026-10-13T14:03:00.000Z request 13: GET /admin/host -> ok, 200 in 9.1 ms (base: 3) \\ ); try expectKept(.{ .since = "2026-10-13T14:02", .until = "2026-10-13T14:03" }, \\ 2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z request 12: POST /gopher/chat/c/1_2/T/upload -> ok, 200 in 41.3 ms (base: 2) \\ upload: 9000 bytes, arrived in 40 ms \\ stream ended: displaced \\ ); // Before any time: the boot's own lines are left out once a time is asked. try expectKept(.{ .until = "2026-10-13T14:02" }, \\ 2026-10-13T14:01:59.900Z request 11: GET /gopher/chat -> ok, 200 in 3.0 ms (base: 1) \\ ); } test "log view: a request by its number, and requests by their path, with the lines under them" { try expectKept(.{ .request = 12 }, \\ 2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z request 12: POST /gopher/chat/c/1_2/T/upload -> ok, 200 in 41.3 ms (base: 2) \\ upload: 9000 bytes, arrived in 40 ms \\ ); try expectKept(.{ .request = 1 }, ""); // 1 is not 11, 12 or 13 try expectKept(.{ .path = "/gopher/chat" }, \\ 2026-10-13T14:01:59.900Z request 11: GET /gopher/chat -> ok, 200 in 3.0 ms (base: 1) \\ 2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z request 12: POST /gopher/chat/c/1_2/T/upload -> ok, 200 in 41.3 ms (base: 2) \\ upload: 9000 bytes, arrived in 40 ms \\ ); try expectKept(.{ .path = "/admin", .since = "2026-10-13T14:02:30" }, \\ 2026-10-13T14:03:00.000Z request 13: GET /admin/host -> ok, 200 in 9.1 ms (base: 3) \\ ); } test "log view: the query's filters, and a value spelled wrong is the client's" { const a = testing.allocator; const f = try parseFilter(a, "/admin/log?since=2026-10-13T14%3A02&request=12&path=%2Fgopher&boot=before"); defer if (f.since) |s| a.free(s); defer if (f.path) |p| a.free(p); try testing.expectEqualStrings("2026-10-13T14:02", f.since.?); try testing.expectEqual(@as(?u64, 12), f.request); try testing.expectEqualStrings("/gopher", f.path.?); try testing.expectEqual(Boot.before, f.boot); const none = try parseFilter(a, "/admin/log"); try testing.expect(!none.any()); try testing.expectEqual(Boot.both, none.boot); for ([_][]const u8{ "?since=yesterday", "?since=2026-1x", "?until=", "?request=", "?request=-1", "?request=+5", "?request=18446744073709551616", "?boot=all", "?path=gopher", "?since=2026-10-13T14:02:07.1234567890Z" }) |q| { const t = try std.fmt.allocPrint(a, "/admin/log{s}", .{q}); defer a.free(t); try testing.expectError(error.BadFilter, parseFilter(a, t)); } try testing.expectError(error.MalformedForm, parseFilter(a, "/admin/log?path=%zz")); } test "log view: a request refused at its head is found by its path, its upload line with it (metal-vmm QUEUE 194.5)" { // The kernel's refusal line carries METHOD PATH, as the route's does // (zig-metal-unikernel request_line.what). const text = \\ 2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z request 20: POST /chat/c/1_2/T/upload (refused at its head) -> every upload slot is held, 503 (base: 2) \\ upload: 2026-10-13T14:02:07.123Z request 20: /chat/c/1_2/T/upload, 0 bytes, not whole after 0 ms, 0 disk requests: busy (503) \\ 2026-10-13T14:02:08.000Z request 21: POST /chat/c/1_2/T/upload -> ok, 200 in 41.3 ms (base: 2) \\ ; var buf: [2048]u8 = undefined; var w: std.Io.Writer = .fixed(&buf); _ = try writeLines(&w, text, .{ .path = "/chat/c/1_2/T/upload" }); try testing.expectEqualStrings(text, w.buffered()); }

name: repos:zig-metal-unikernel/src/pci.zig
html: //! **THE PCI BUS: HOW A PC SAYS WHAT IS PLUGGED INTO IT.** QEMU's microvm puts //! each device at an address you are told in advance; a PC, and so a //! DigitalOcean droplet, puts them in numbered slots and expects you to ask. //! Every slot answers through two I/O ports: write which slot and register to //! 0xCF8, read the answer at 0xCFC. A slot with nothing in it answers 0xFFFF //! as its vendor. //! //! Each device's registers say who made it, what it is, where its memory //! windows (BARs) were put by the BIOS, and a chain of **capabilities**: //! small records that, for a virtio device, say which window holds which of //! its controls. This file reads all of that and knows nothing about virtio. //! //! Configuration mechanism #1 of the PCI Local Bus Specification 3.0, §3.2.2.3.2; //! bus 0 only, because a droplet has one bus and no bridges. const props = @import("coverage"); const port = @import("port.zig"); const address_port: u16 = 0xCF8; const data_port: u16 = 0xCFC; /// One function in one slot on bus 0. pub const Function = struct { slot: u8, function: u8, fn address(self: Function, register: u8) u32 { return 0x8000_0000 | (@as(u32, self.slot) << 11) | (@as(u32, self.function) << 8) | (register & 0xFC); } pub fn read32(self: Function, register: u8) u32 { port.outl(address_port, self.address(register)); return port.inl(data_port); } pub fn read16(self: Function, register: u8) u16 { return @truncate(self.read32(register) >> @intCast((register & 2) * 8)); } pub fn read8(self: Function, register: u8) u8 { return @truncate(self.read32(register) >> @intCast((register & 3) * 8)); } pub fn write16(self: Function, register: u8, value: u16) void { port.outl(address_port, self.address(register)); port.outw(data_port + (register & 2), value); } pub fn vendor(self: Function) u16 { return self.read16(0x00); } pub fn device(self: Function) u16 { return self.read16(0x02); } pub fn subsystem(self: Function) u16 { return self.read16(0x2E); } /// **A DEVICE MAY NOT TOUCH MEMORY UNTIL IT IS TOLD IT MAY.** Bit 1 lets /// us reach its windows; bit 2 (bus master) lets it read and write ours, /// which is how a virtqueue works at all. QEMU refuses a device's memory /// accesses without it, so a forgotten bit 2 is a request that never /// completes. pub fn enable(self: Function) void { self.write16(0x04, self.read16(0x04) | 0x0006); } /// The physical address a BAR was given, or null for an I/O-port BAR or /// an empty one. A 64-bit BAR takes the next register for its top half. pub fn bar(self: Function, index: u8) ?u64 { if (index > 5) { props.reachable(@src(), "pci: a BAR past the sixth", null); return null; } const register = 0x10 + index * 4; const low = self.read32(register); if (low & 1 != 0) { props.reachable(@src(), "pci: an I/O-space BAR, which this driver does not map", null); return null; // I/O space } var at: u64 = low & 0xFFFF_FFF0; if ((low >> 1) & 3 == 2) { if (index == 5) { props.reachable(@src(), "pci: a 64-bit BAR in the last slot, with no register for its top half", null); return null; } at |= @as(u64, self.read32(register + 4)) << 32; } return if (at == 0) null else at; } /// The capability list, if the device has one: status bit 4 says so, and /// register 0x34 points at the first record. pub fn capabilities(self: Function) Capabilities { const has = self.read16(0x06) & 0x10 != 0; return .{ .function = self, .next = if (has) self.read8(0x34) & 0xFC else 0 }; } }; pub const Capabilities = struct { function: Function, next: u8, /// A record's id, and where it starts in configuration space. A list that /// loops is stopped after 48 records: there is room for no more. seen: u8 = 0, pub fn nextOne(self: *Capabilities) ?struct { id: u8, at: u8 } { if (self.next == 0 or self.seen == 48) return null; const at = self.next; self.seen += 1; self.next = self.function.read8(at + 1) & 0xFC; return .{ .id = self.function.read8(at), .at = at }; } }; /// Whether a vendor id means a device is there. **NOBODY IS EITHER ALL ONES /// OR ALL ZEROES**: a real bus with an empty slot reads 0xFFFF, and a machine /// with no bus at all may answer either (QEMU's microvm reads 0xFFFF; /// metal-vmm answers every port it does not model with zeroes).
